newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission would hold its weekly meeting on Thursday instead of Wednesday due to the EU/Japan summit taking place in The Hague on Wednesday and to the U.N. General Assembly session on the environment to take place in New York next week.
Vale de Almeida said the Denver G7 summit conclusions were available to reporters in spokeman Nikolaus van der Pas's office.

He said South Africa had made new proposals to the EU regarding an EU/South Africa bilateral trade agreement. He said the proposals were too general and that the EU was expecting supplementary input to resume negotiations. A ministerial meeting will take place on July 18, Vale de Almeida added.

In answer to a question, Vale de Almeida said the examination procedure initiated by the Commission into obstacles in the U.S. to the licensing of music concerned all European authors and not only Irish music rights.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/548: Commission opens in depth inquiry into Guiness/Grand Metropolitan merger.
- IP/97/549: Commission challenges U.S. exceptions to authors exclusive rights.
- IP/97/550: European Commission and South Africa pursue technical discussions for bilateral agreement.
- IP/97/551: Denver Summit (June 20-22, 1997) - Statement by Jacques Santer, President of the European Commission.
- IP/97/552: Final adoption of the new "Television without Frontiers" directive.
- Speech/97/144: Speech by Commissioner Hans van den Broek on "The rule of Law in the context of enlargement".
- Memo/97/63: The new "Television without Frontiers" directive.
- Agenda of the European Commission visit to the Luxembourg Presidency on July 3rd, 1997.
